Let’s dive into Chapter 4: Adapting Communication—Speaking Each Color’s Language.
Once you’ve spotted the different colors in people’s personalities, the real magic happens when you start adjusting the way you communicate. Think of it like tuning a radio—if you’re on the right frequency, your message comes through crystal clear. Instead of waiting for others to change, you’re the one meeting them where they are.
So, let’s talk about how to connect with each color, starting with the Reds.
Reds are all about action. They want things fast, clear, and straight to the point. If you’re talking with a Red, skip the small talk and focus on results. They respect when you’re confident and decisive, so don’t be afraid to share your opinion and stand by it.
Here are some tips for reaching Reds:
Be direct and concise. Focus on goals and the outcomes that matter. And show you’re ready to take action.
For example, if you’re pitching an idea to a Red manager, just lay out the main benefits, the results you’re aiming for, and the next steps. Save the backstory and emotional appeals for another time.
Now, let’s move to Yellows.
Yellows thrive on energy and connection. They love lively discussions, creative brainstorming, and a good dose of positive feedback. If you want to engage with a Yellow, bring some enthusiasm—share stories, use expressive language, and don’t be afraid to crack a joke.
Here’s how to connect with Yellows:
Use humor and colorful language. Encourage sharing of ideas. And always recognize their contributions.
In team meetings, Yellows shine when they’re involved early on. Their creativity can really take things to the next level. Just remember—you might need to gently guide the conversation back if it starts to wander.
Next up, Greens.
Greens appreciate patience and harmony. They prefer calm, steady conversations and really dislike being rushed or put on the spot. When you’re working with a Green, take the time to listen, acknowledge their efforts, and offer reassurance.
Some tips for connecting with Greens:
Be patient and supportive. Avoid confrontation or sudden changes. And emphasize working together as a team.
Picture introducing a new process at work—the best way with a Green is to give them time to adjust, explain things clearly, and let them know you see and appreciate their contributions.
Finally, let’s talk about Blues.
Blues want information, structure, and accuracy. They value details, logical arguments, and time to process decisions. When talking with a Blue, come prepared with facts, answer their questions fully, and don’t rush them through their analysis.
Here’s what works best for Blues:
Provide data and evidence. Be precise and organized. And make sure there’s time for careful consideration.
So, if you’re discussing a project with a Blue, bring the relevant documents, clearly outline each step, and welcome their questions. Try to avoid vague statements or purely emotional arguments—they want the facts.
Now, you might wonder—does adapting your style mean you’re being fake? Not at all. It’s more like learning a few phrases in someone else’s language so they feel welcome in your space. The more flexible you become, the easier it gets to build trust and keep misunderstandings to a minimum.
But here’s something to pay attention to—self-awareness. It’s totally normal to slip back into your own style, especially when things get stressful. The real growth comes when you make a conscious choice to adjust and bridge the gap. That’s how you create stronger, more productive, and more harmonious connections with everyone around you.
